mappings.note: What the nucleus contains -- chromosomes carrying the DNA. The gene-on-chromosome basis of inheritance, LO-2.
Animals whose offspring sex is not set genetically (temperature-dependent). Cited to the sex-determination outcome LO-3, which this contrasts with.
Probability of a boy is one half. Human sex determination, LO-3.
Females have the matched XX pair. Human sex determination, LO-3.
Why variation is built into reproduction -- DNA copying errors and sexual recombination. The origin of the variation LO-1 says accumulates.
Natural selection and genetic drift altering the frequency of an inherited trait. Variation feeding evolution, LO-1 of C 4.5.
Tails cut off squirrels do not affect the progeny, because only germ-cell DNA is passed on. Inheritance through genes, LO-2 -- not C 4.5-LO-1, since nothing accumulates here.
Who the theory of evolution is associated with. Pure attribution, which no learning outcome covers -- C 4.5-LO-1 is about variation accumulating -- so the evolution competency is cited.
Which of the listed items counts as a characteristic. The trait concept underlying LO-2; options are not printed but the subject is fixed by the stem.
Mendel worked on the garden pea. Naming the organism is not applying his laws to a cross, so the C 4.4 competency rather than LO-1.

Why the pea suited the experiment -- clear contrasting characters, true-breeding lines, short generations, controllable pollination. This is experimental design, C 8.2 (its LO-3 is specifically Punnett squares, which this is not), with C 4.4 for the Mendelian context.
The trait appearing in the first generation is the dominant one. LO-2 of C 4.4 verbatim.
Dominant and recessive explained through a monohybrid cross. LO-2, which is about distinguishing them using a given cross.
True/false on a recessive factor being lost -- it is hidden, not destroyed. Dominant versus recessive, LO-2.
Matches four pea characters to their dominant form. Dominant versus recessive, LO-2.
A human female is XX. Sex determination, LO-3.
Why the mother cannot determine the child's sex. LO-3, including its social point.
Full account of human sex determination and the consequences of misunderstanding it. LO-3 in full.
A human male is XY. Sex determination, LO-3.
Probability of a fourth daughter is still one half. The independence of each fertilisation in human sex determination, LO-3; no Punnett grid is asked for, so not C 8.2-LO-3.
Labelled diagram of human sex determination showing where the outcome is decided. LO-3.
Twenty-three pairs of chromosomes in a human body cell. The chromosomal basis of inheritance, LO-2.
How DNA, genes and chromosomes relate. LO-2's core.
True/false on a gamete having 46 chromosomes. Chromosome number and the halving at gamete formation, LO-2.
Matches gene, chromosome, gamete and zygote to their descriptions. LO-2's vocabulary.
The 3:1 second-generation ratio of a monohybrid cross. Predicting the ratio, LO-1 of C 4.4.
The 1:2:1 genotype ratio behind the 3:1 phenotype ratio. LO-1 for the ratio and LO-2 because the point is genotype versus phenotype.
Works a monohybrid cross from pure parents to the second generation. Applying Mendel's law and predicting the ratio, LO-1; no grid is demanded, so C 8.2-LO-3 is left out.
True/false on two hybrid talls giving short offspring. The second-generation outcome of a monohybrid cross, LO-1.
The whole monohybrid experiment: crosses, results, conclusions. LO-1 for the ratios, LO-2 for the dominant/recessive conclusion it establishes.
Expected short plants among 1600 in the second generation. Applying the predicted 3:1 ratio, LO-1.
Draws the labelled cross grid to the second generation showing every genotype. Drawing the square to predict the outcome is C 8.2-LO-3; the Mendelian ratio it yields is LO-1.
States the law of segregation. Cited to LO-1, the only outcome covering Mendel's laws; the law is inseparable from the monohybrid cross it explains.
Argues from the reappearance of short plants that the recessive factor survived the first generation. That is the dominant/recessive point of LO-2, argued from the LO-1 ratios.
A gamete carries one set of chromosomes. The chromosomal basis of inheritance, LO-2.
A single chromosome set means haploid. LO-2's vocabulary.
What determines a child's sex. LO-3 verbatim.
Assertion-reason on the mother determining sex -- the assertion is false while the reason is true. Sex determination, LO-3.
Why variations accumulate over generations. LO-1 of C 4.5 verbatim.
How variation compounds over generations and why that matters. LO-1 of C 4.5.
Weighs fidelity of inheritance against variation for survival in a changing environment. The variation-to-evolution link of LO-1.
What carrying two recessive factors implies about the plant. Genotype versus phenotype, LO-2 of C 4.4.
How a gene controls height through an enzyme and a hormone. The gene-to-trait mechanism of LO-2, not the cross ratios of C 4.4.
Puts Mendel's two laws on a chromosomal footing. The chromosome mechanics are LO-2 of C 3.3; the laws themselves are LO-1 of C 4.4.
Definition of heredity as transmission of characters through DNA in the gametes. LO-2.
Assertion-reason tying family resemblance to DNA passed through gametes. LO-2.
Heredity, the mechanism of transmission, and inherited versus acquired traits. All LO-2; nothing here concerns crosses or ratios.
Why an acquired trait is not inherited -- germ-cell DNA is unchanged. LO-2.
Assertion-reason on acquired traits being passed on -- false assertion, true reason. LO-2.
Definition of a recessive trait. LO-2 of C 4.4.
Mendel's 'factor' is today's gene, a segment of DNA on a chromosome. The gene concept, LO-2 of C 3.3, rather than the application of his laws.
Factors are now called genes. Same reading as 707239, LO-2.
Two sources of variation -- copying errors and recombination. The origin of accumulating variation, LO-1 of C 4.5.
True/false on identical twins showing no genetic variation. Sources and limits of variation, LO-1 of C 4.5.
The law of independent assortment and the dihybrid evidence for it. Mendel's laws applied to a dihybrid cross, LO-1.
Assertion-reason on shape and colour being inherited together -- false, by independent assortment. LO-1's dihybrid half.
Mendel's dihybrid cross and what it established. LO-1 verbatim.
Completes the 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio. Predicting the ratio, LO-1.
Splits 640 second-generation seeds by the 9:3:3:1 ratio. Applying the predicted dihybrid ratio, LO-1.
